outcome: Neonatal transition (Apgar score, arterial oxygen saturation, heart rate, temperature)
Neonatal stress response (salivary free cortisol, salivary alpha amylase)
Maternal stress response (salivary free cortisol, salivary alpha amylase)
finding: Early SSC after cesarean section did not significantly affect neonatal transition, neonatal or maternal stress response, or maternal pain and wellbeing, although a greater rise in maternal salivary alpha-amylase immediately after delivery was observed in the early SSC group.
mod_finding: Early skin-to-skin contact (SSC) after cesarean section did not negatively impact neonatal transition or maternal outcomes, although a greater increase in maternal salivary alpha-amylase post-delivery suggests potential stress from early SSC.
